contributions.statement: Write observability into the spec as checkable acceptance criteria (which fields and correlation IDs must be logged on dependency failure, timeout, or validation rejection) and verify with fault-injection smoke tests, because agent-generated services exposed a fault-specific log signal for only 5-14% of injected faults.
contributions.evidence: §IV-B Table III: FSR 4.95-13.99% across three frontier models over 1,615 fault instances per model on 200 spec-generated Kubernetes systems; custom log oracles may miss indirect signals.

contributions.statement: Do not add a generic 'improve observability' instruction to agent prompts: it more than doubled logging statements (4.9 vs 2.1) while diagnostic-content precision fell (KeyBag P 0.33 to 0.20, F1 0.36 to 0.26).
contributions.evidence: §IV-A Fig. 4, Table II; five repeats claimed but only means shown; ground truth is human-written logging.

reason: No other KB paper measures whether agent-written code is diagnosable; both the low fault-signal rate and the quantity-over-quality effect of explicit logging prompts are actionable for delivery services. The skill result is weak and excluded.
